entities.summary:
Antonio Barberini (1615-1671): A pivotal figure in the House of Barberini and a key player in 17th-century European politics.

As an Italian Catholic cardinal, Archbishop of Reims, and military leader, Barberini played a significant role at several papal conclaves of the century. His brother Cardinal Francesco Barberini and Taddeo Barberini joined him in shaping the politics, religion, art, and music of 17th-century Italy.

Barberini's patronage of the arts, particularly under French influence, helped establish Reims Cathedral as a prominent cultural center. He was also involved in several significant military campaigns, including the Italian Wars and the Franco-Dutch War.

As the cardinal-nephew of Pope Urban VIII, Barberini supported France and helped secure its role in European politics during this period.

His legacy extends to the transformation of Reims Cathedral into a symbol of French Catholicism and his contributions to the development of Baroque art and architecture.
